name: Wagga Wagga Botanic Gardens
note: Public gardens (8 ha) with the Wagga Wagga Zoo, a free flight aviary and the Willans Hill miniature railway; a park with attractions inside.

name: Willans Hill Miniature Railway
note: Ride-on miniature railway (operator-run) in the Botanic Gardens, open 1st and 3rd Sunday of the month only; a vehicle-type attraction at a fixed place.

name: Museum of the Riverina
note: Regional museum (historic council chambers site and Botanic Gardens site) on the district's history.

name: RAAF Wagga Aviation Heritage Centre
note: Aviation heritage museum in the old guard house at the RAAF Base Wagga entrance, showing the air force's history in the Riverina; free entry, limited hours.

name: Wagga Beach
note: Sand beach on the Murrumbidgee River in Cabarita Park, a swimming spot in the city.

name: Wagga Wagga Art Gallery
note: Public art gallery (free entry) in the Civic Centre, with the national art glass collection and Australian print collection.

name: Wagga Wagga Rail Heritage Museum
note: Small railway heritage museum in the Porter's Room at the Wagga railway station, Monday mornings only.

name: Charles Sturt University Winery
note: University winery with cellar door sales and tastings (operator venue, not a standalone attraction; judge as a winery).

name: Wiradjuri Walking Track
note: Riverside walking track in Wagga Wagga with maps at the visitor centre; a walk, no point coordinates yet.
coordinates_source: osm:Wiradjuri Walking Track (a point on the track)

name: Wollundry Track
note: Walking track around Wollundry Lagoon in Wagga Wagga, with maps at the visitor centre.

name: Wagga Wagga Heritage Walk
note: Self-guided heritage walk through central Wagga Wagga's historic buildings, with maps from the visitor centre.

name: The Rock (Hanging Rock Hill)
note: Granite monolith (Hanging Rock Hill) with a roughly 6 km walk to the top and views over the Riverina, 6 km west of The Rock township.

name: Ladysmith Tourist Railway
note: Tourist railway (volunteer-run) at Ladysmith, 20 minutes east of Wagga; open days only on the second Saturday of the month.

name: Riverina Outdoor Art Trail
note: Outdoor art trail of murals and sculptures linking Wagga Wagga and Griffith; a route of many small stops rather than one place.

name: Albury Library Museum
note: Museum, library and gallery exhibition space in one building on Kiewa Street, Albury (civic building with public museum and gallery).

name: Albury Botanic Gardens
note: Public botanic gardens on Wodonga Place, Albury, in the town centre.

name: Murray Art Museum Albury
note: Regional art museum (MAMA) on Dean Street, Albury, with changing exhibitions.

name: Hume Dam
note: Large dam wall on the Murray River, open to walk across, with a viewing platform, picnic area and small open-air museum; free.

name: Lake Hume
note: Man-made reservoir (Lake Hume, behind Hume Dam) for swimming, boating, kayaking and birdwatching, around Lake Hume Village.

name: Nail Can Hill
note: Hill and walking track just west of central Albury, with a lookout over the city.

name: High Country Rail Trail
note: Rail trail from Albury along Lake Hume towards Tallangatta (Victoria); a long cycling and walking route, starts at the Albury visitor centre.

name: Albury Swim Centre
note: Council public swimming centre with three pools and a three-storey water slide (operator-run leisure facility).

name: Woomargama National Park
note: National park, the largest protected forest west of the Great Dividing Range near Holbrook and Albury; camping, hiking and 4WD touring.

name: Holbrook Submarine Institution
note: Submarine museum at Holbrook, a named attraction of the town in Wikivoyage's Riverina and Holbrook listings; visitor access and hours unverified.

name: Corowa Federation Museum
note: Museum on Queen Street, Corowa, about the 1893 Federation Conference and the town's history.

name: Sanger Street Federation Precinct (Oddfellows Hall and Globe Hotel)
note: Historic street precinct of 19th-century buildings tied to the Federation conventions: Oddfellows Hall (where public meetings were held, interior run by council) and the Globe Hotel; a walking stop.

name: Murray to the Mountains Rail Trail
wiki: Murray to the Mountains Rail Trail
note: Rail trail connecting Corowa to Rutherglen (Victorian section); a long cycling and walking route with no single point.

name: Corowa Flour Mill
note: Historic flour mill building in Corowa, a heritage site (listed as a tourist attraction on Wikipedia only; public access unverified).

name: Narrandera Flora and Fauna Reserve
note: River red gum reserve on the Murrumbidgee where koalas are regularly seen, reached by a dirt trail from the town; a wildlife walk.
coordinates_source: osm:Murrumbidgee Valley Nature Reserve (name match to confirm against the koala reserve)

name: Narrandera Parkside Cottage Museum
note: Heritage museum in Parkside Cottage with a merino clock and equipment from Robert Falcon Scott's Antarctic expedition.

name: Big Guitar (Narrandera)
note: Giant playable guitar at the Narrandera Visitor Information Centre, a roadside big thing that visitors photograph.

name: Narrandera Skywalk
note: Elevated walkway over the Murrumbidgee River in Narrandera, a short walk with river views.

name: Lake Talbot Water Park
note: Council water park on Lake Talbot with water slides, splash park and lake swimming (operator-run leisure facility).

name: Griffith Pioneer Park Museum
note: Open-air heritage museum with 40+ heritage buildings and a Italian immigrant section on Remembrance Drive, Griffith.

name: Cocoparra National Park
note: National park of gorges and a rugged range 30-40 minutes from Griffith, with the Jacks Creek, Falcon Falls and Store Creek walks and spring wildflowers.

name: Scenic Hill Lookout
note: Lookout over Griffith's vineyards, citrus orchards and irrigation channels; a short drive to a viewpoint.
coordinates_source: osm:Scenic Hill Reserve (reserve centroid; lookout point to confirm)

name: Italian Heritage Trail (Griffith)
note: Heritage walking trail through Griffith tracing the Italian immigrant families who shaped the city.

name: De Bortoli Winery
note: Large family winery at Bilbul near Griffith with cellar door and tastings (operator venue; judge as a winery, not a standalone spot); location not yet confirmed.

name: Yarran Wines
note: Cellar door winery at Myall Park, Yenda, with free tastings and cheese platters (operator venue); location not yet confirmed.

name: Big Wine Barrel (Griffith)
note: Giant wine barrel roadside landmark in Griffith; seen only in a regional news article (no visitor-guide source yet); location not confirmed.

name: Fivebough and Tuckerbil Wetlands
note: Wetlands reserve beside Leeton with boardwalks and walking trails, a birdwatching site.

name: Middle Beach (Murrumbidgee River)
note: Sandy beach on the Murrumbidgee River in Murrumbidgee Valley National Park, reached by an unsealed track from Yanco; a swimming and camping spot.

name: Roxy Theatre (Leeton)
note: Art Deco heritage theatre on Leeton's main street, neon-lit at night; Wikivoyage says the interior was closed for renovation as of 2023, so public access is unverified.

name: Yanco Powerhouse Museum
note: Museum in a former 1913 power house at Yanco, open the last Sunday of the month, on the M.I.A. irrigation history.

name: Whitton Malt House
note: Working malt house at Whitton near Leeton where visitors can see grain malting up close (agritourism operator).

name: Southern Cotton Gin
note: Cotton gin near Leeton open to visitors to see cotton processing (agritourism operator).

name: Leeton Art Deco Architecture
note: Town-centre Art Deco streetscape of shopfronts and water towers at Chelmsford Place, a walking stop rather than one place.

name: Leeton Gliding Club
note: Gliding club at Brobenah airfield 9 km north of Leeton (club operator; flights are arranged, not a drop-in attraction).

name: LillyPilly Estate Winery
note: Cellar door winery near Leeton (operator venue; judge as a winery).

name: Toorak Winery
note: Cellar door winery on Toorak Road, Leeton (operator venue; judge as a winery).

name: Leeton Farmers Markets
note: Monthly farmers market at Mountford Park on the first Saturday of the month (a market that runs one day a month).

name: Australian Art Deco Festival (Leeton)
note: Annual festival held at Chelmsford Place, Leeton (an event, not a permanent place).

name: Hay Gaol
note: Former colonial gaol on Church Street, Hay, converted into a museum (open daily, paid entry).

name: ShearOutback (Shearers Hall of Fame)
note: Shearers' Hall of Fame museum at Hay with daily live shearing demonstrations and a cafe, on the Sturt Highway roundabout.

name: Dunera Museum
note: Museum at Hay Railway Station about the Dunera ship and the internment of WWII refugees and prisoners at Hay.

name: Hay Water Towers Mural
note: Mural on Hay's water towers commemorating the Great Emu War and other wars; a street-art stop, not a memorial site.

name: Hay Plain
note: Flat, treeless plain west of Hay, a landscape drive known for emus and big sunsets (Visit Hay); a region, not one site, so no point coordinate.

name: Bidgee Riverside Trail
note: Riverside walking and cycling trail beside the Murrumbidgee at Hay.

name: Balranald Discovery Centre
note: Visitor information centre with a history discovery centre and cafe on Market Street, Balranald.

name: Balranald Southern Cross Museum
note: Small aviation and history museum with a replica of the Southern Cross, gold coin donation.

name: Malcolm Building Museum
note: Small museum of historic photos and artefacts in Balranald, entered through the Discovery Centre (near-duplicate of the Discovery Centre stop).

name: Balranald Heritage and Historical Trail
note: Walking trail of about 1.5 hours through Balranald's historic buildings starting at the Discovery Centre.

name: Yanga National Park
note: National park beside Balranald on the Murrumbidgee, with Yanga Lake, camping and historic station buildings; birdwatching and fishing.

name: Yanga Homestead
note: Restored 1870 pastoral homestead inside Yanga National Park with self-guided tours and stables and station buildings.

name: Yanga Woolshed
note: Late 19th-century woolshed, once the largest in the Lower Darling region, with a platform over the Murrumbidgee.

name: Yanga Lake Circuit
note: One-kilometre family loop walk around Yanga Lake in Yanga National Park with birdwatching; a track inside the park.

name: Murrumbidgee Valley National Park
note: Riverside national park between Narrandera, Hay and Balranald with river camping, fishing, kayaking and birdwatching, few facilities.

name: Murray Valley National Park
note: Red gum forest national park along the Murray (Ramsar wetlands) with camping, birdwatching, fishing and kayaking.

name: Willandra National Park
note: Pastoral-heritage national park on the Willandra Creek with self-drive, cycling and walking routes (overlaps the Outback brief's Willandra Lakes; judge in one place).

name: Junction Park (Murray and Darling confluence)
note: Park and lookout at Wentworth where the Murray and Darling rivers meet, one of the country's best-known river junctions.

name: Old Wentworth Gaol
note: Heritage-listed single-storey brick gaol (1879-81) now a museum on Beverley Street, Wentworth.

name: Perry Sandhills
note: Large sand dunes on Renmark Road near Wentworth, a quiet place to walk and climb the dunes.

name: Saint Ignatius School Museum
note: Former Catholic school (1911-12), an unusual weatherboard building now a museum in Wentworth.

name: Wentworth Pioneer Museum
note: Small museum of colonial and river life on the Murray in Wentworth, with extinct-animal replicas.

name: Dog on the Tuckerbox
note: Bronze statue of a dog on a tuckerbox at Snake Gully, 5 miles north of Gundagai beside the Hume Highway, with an interpretive walk; free, about 30 minutes.

name: Rusconi's Marble Cathedral
note: Marble model of a cathedral made from 20,948 pieces of NSW marble by sculptor Frank Rusconi, on show in the Gundagai Visitor Centre for a small fee.

name: Gundagai Museum
note: Local museum of tools and farm machinery in Gundagai (9am-3pm).

name: Prince Alfred Bridge
note: Timber bridge of 1866 over the Murrumbidgee, billed as Australia's longest timber bridge, a historic structure to walk or view.

name: Gundagai Railway Museum
note: Railway museum in Gundagai with a self-guided tour from the visitor centre website; open-hours unverified.
coordinates_source: osm:Gundagai Railway Station (museum location to confirm)

name: Gundagai Architectural Heritage Walk
note: Self-guided two-kilometre heritage walk through Gundagai's historic buildings, with the Gabriel Gallery of 1900s glass-plate photographs nearby.

name: Gundagai War Memorials (WWI to Boer War)
note: Group of war memorials in Gundagai (WWI and II, Vietnam, Korea, Boer War); minor memorials listed by Wikivoyage with no visitor draw of their own.

name: Snake Gully Cup and Dog on the Tuckerbox Festival
note: Annual two-day horse-racing carnival in November, an event with no permanent place.

name: Turning Wave Festival (Gundagai)
note: Annual Irish-Australian festival in Gundagai in September, an event.

name: Pioneer Women's Hut Museum
note: Pioneer women's hut museum 9 km west of Tumbarumba on Tumbarumba Road, open Wednesday and weekends.

name: Tumbarumba–Rosewood Rail Trail
note: 21 km rail trail (opened 2020) on the former Tumbarumba branch line through scenic countryside, for walking and cycling.
coordinates_source: osm:Tumbarumba to Rosewood Rail Trail (trailhead at Tumbarumba)

name: Tumbafest
note: Annual town festival in late February with music, wine and market stalls (an event).

name: Paddys River Falls
note: Waterfall listed on Wikipedia in the Riverina category; no visitor-guide source in this region run, so its location and access need confirming (may belong to the Snowy brief).

name: Bradman's Birthplace Museum
note: Museum in the cottage at 89 Adams Street where Sir Donald Bradman was born, with memorabilia (paid entry).

name: Cricket Captains Walk
note: Free 200 m walk in Cootamundra with bronze busts of every Australian Test captain and a life-size bronze Bradman, 24 hours a day.

name: Stockinbingal Heritage Walk
note: Self-guided walk through the village of Stockinbingal near Cootamundra on pioneer family life; a village walk.

name: Roundhouse Museum
note: Railway roundhouse museum in Junee with a collection of engines and carriages, once the largest roundhouse in the Southern Hemisphere, many open to explore.

name: Junee Licorice Factory
note: Licorice and chocolate factory on Lord Street, Junee, where visitors watch making on weekdays, make their own sweets and buy from the shop (a shop-and-factory visit).

name: Broadway Museum (Junee)
note: Small museum on Broadway, Junee (daily 10 am to 4 pm).

name: Monte Cristo Homestead
note: Homestead in Junee run as a haunted house attraction; Wikivoyage says the house is poorly maintained and much of it closed, a marginal kitsch stop.

name: Athenium Theatre
note: Restored heritage theatre in Junee with performances (a venue for shows, not a daily visit).

name: Bethungra Spiral
note: Railway spiral engineered to lift the line over the Bethungra Range near Junee; a viewpoint stop for train watchers.

name: Coolamon Fire Museum
note: Museum of fire-fighting equipment on Loughnan Street, Coolamon (10 am-4 pm).

name: Up-To-Date Store (Coolamon)
note: Local cultural precinct with several small attractions and a shop in Coolamon, free entry.

name: Temora Aviation Museum
note: Aviation museum at Temora Airport with warbirds that fly, a large collection and VR exhibits; the town's headline attraction.

name: Temora Rural Museum
note: Rural and agricultural museum in the Bundawarrah Centre, Temora, on the Riverina's farming history.

name: Greens Gunyah Museum
note: Museum in Lockhart with a wool art gallery and collections of the verandah town's history.

name: Lockhart Water Tower Mural
note: Mural on Lockhart's water tower of brolgas and a waterfall, a street-art stop.

name: Galore Hill Nature Reserve
note: Nature reserve about 15 km north of Lockhart, walks and bush scenery; no visitor infrastructure described.

name: Lockhart District War Memorial
note: Town war memorial in Lockhart, a minor memorial.

name: Tocumwal Historic Aerodrome
note: Former WWII US Army Air Forces base on Burma Road with surviving runways and hangars, a gliding and aerobatic-championship venue; hangar tours and events vary.

name: Tocumwal Town Beach
note: Large Murray River beach beside Tocumwal in red gum forest, popular for swimming and camping; unpatrolled.

name: The Big Cod (Tocumwal)
note: Giant fibreglass Murray cod on the Tocumwal foreshore, installed 1968, a roadside big thing.

name: Tocumwal Railway Station
note: Closed-to-passengers railway station with a former change-of-gauge history; now a freight point, no public visitor facility.

name: Moama Holden Motor Museum
note: Holden car museum at Moama, the one attraction Wikivoyage lists for the town; opening times unverified.

name: Murray Downs Homestead
note: Heritage homestead (Murray Downs, Wikipedia article); its coordinates sit about 80 km north of Balranald, not at Moama, so the location and visitor access need confirming.

name: The Great Aussie Beer Shed (Moama)
note: Beer hall and entertainment venue at Moama (a bar and restaurant venue, judge as a venue).

name: Coleambally Bucyrus Dragline
note: Working 1935 American dragline excavator in Lions Park at Coleambally's entrance, one of four machines that dug the irrigation channels; a big machine stop, no coordinates yet.
coordinates_source: osm:Coleambally Lions Park (dragline sits in the park)

name: Coleambally Wineglass Water Tower
note: Water tower decorated with over 64,000 glass tiles in 2008 near Brolga Place, Coleambally, a distinctive roadside landmark.

name: Darlington Point Murrumbidgee Valley Regional Park
note: Small regional park on the Murrumbidgee's northern bank at Darlington Point, picnic spots only; few tourist facilities.

name: Lake Urana
note: Lake near Urana in the Riverina, a nature reserve setting; no visitor-guide source in this run.

name: Big Tennis Racquet (Barellan)
note: Giant tennis racquet roadside big thing at Barellan; one regional news source only.

name: Biggest Football (Ungarie)
note: 800 kg fibreglass Sherrin in Bing Wallder Park at Ungarie, honouring the Daniher brothers; a roadside big thing listed by NSW tourism (Riverina edge of Bland Shire).

name: Lake Mulwala
note: Weir-formed lake on the Murray near Mulwala (NSW side) for boating and water sports; no visitor-guide source read yet.

name: Waring Gardens (Deniliquin)
note: Heritage-listed public gardens in Cressy Street, Deniliquin, with a bandstand and pavilion; a town park.

name: Deni Ute Muster (Play on the Plains)
note: Annual festival in Deniliquin (September/October) with a large ute muster; an event with no permanent place.
